subject.title: [Security] Missing complexity validation and rate limiting on log query filters

question: Should repeated authenticated replay of an already-known ACP session receive additional defense-in-depth limits despite the reported arbitrary-filter path being absent and authenticated callers belonging to the trusted-operator boundary?
rationale: Source inspection disproves the described query-filter mechanism, but only maintainers can decide whether the remaining authenticated replay availability concern merits hardening beyond the documented trust model and existing lifecycle limits.

options.title: Require measured replay proof
options.body: Keep the issue pending a current-main PoC that quantifies CPU, event-loop delay, SQLite contention, or replay latency before adding another limiter.

options.title: Add defense-in-depth now
options.body: Sponsor a focused replay concurrency or request-rate cap with compatibility tests even without a demonstrated security-boundary bypass.

options.title: Close as no-action
options.body: Treat authenticated replay availability as within the trusted-operator model unless new evidence demonstrates a supported-boundary impact.

recommendation.title: Require measured replay proof
recommendation.body: Keep the issue pending a current-main PoC that quantifies CPU, event-loop delay, SQLite contention, or replay latency before adding another limiter.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal is the existing ACP lifecycle flooding and rate-limit hardening commit.
